chunks: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
'O Ali! There is no poverty more intense than ignorance, and there is no wealth more assisting than the intellect.'

key_terms.الْجَهْلُ: Ignorance (jahl) — in Islamic ethics, not merely lack of information but a moral failing that blinds one to truth and virtue
key_terms.الْعَقْلُ: Intellect/reason (aql) — in Shia theology, the divine faculty enabling spiritual perception; Al-Kafi opens with an entire chapter on its supreme importance
key_terms.فَقْرٌ: Poverty (faqr) — material destitution; here used metaphorically for spiritual/intellectual destitution
key_terms.مَالٌ: Wealth (mal) — material property; here used metaphorically for spiritual/intellectual richness

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say to Imam Ali about poverty and ignorance?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) addresses Imam Ali (AS) directly, presenting a powerful chiasmus: the worst poverty is not material destitution but ignorance, while the greatest wealth is not material abundance but the intellect. This saying was transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting the Shia theological emphasis on 'aql (reason/intellect) as the supreme human faculty. The original audience — Shia scholars and students — would have understood 'aql not merely as individual reasoning but as the divinely-endowed capacity for spiritual and moral discernment that guides one toward truth.
